landing.title: See what has grown in your district, season after season.
landing.lead: AgriSense reads public historical crop records for your district and shows which crops have been grown there in each season, alongside current weather. The guide is a starting point for your own judgement, not a prediction.
landing.step1Body: Pick your state and district. You can add a field with just a name and its area in acres.
landing.step2Body: AgriSense looks at which crops covered the most area in your district in this season over past years, giving recent years more weight.
landing.step3Title: You see the guide and the weather
landing.step3Body: You get a ranked list of historically grown crops with the years covered, plus a weather snapshot with its source and time.
landing.honestTitle: What AgriSense is, and is not
landing.honest1: It shows historical prevalence: how much of the recorded cropped area in your district each crop has held.
landing.honest2: It does not predict yield, price or how well a crop will do on your field.
landing.honest3: Soil test values are optional and are not used by the Regional Crop Guide.
landing.honest4: Every guide shows the years it covers and its limits, so you can judge how far to rely on it.
landing.featTitle: Everything in one place, nothing overstated
landing.feat1Body: Crops ranked by how much of your district's recorded cropped area they held in each season, with the years covered.
landing.feat2Body: Current conditions and a 7-day forecast, labelled live, cached or unavailable, with the source and time.
landing.feat3Body: A model ranks crops from seven values you enter.
landing.feat4Body: A short, sourced checklist for a crop, built from the guide's data and official resources.
landing.feat5Body: Heads-up notices about weather that may matter for your fields.
landing.feat6Body: Links to the official portals for soil health, crop insurance and farmer support.
landing.ctaBody: Create an account, choose your district and see the guide in under a minute.

how.title: What the Regional Crop Guide shows
how.lead: A plain-language account of where the numbers come from and what they cannot tell you.
how.whatTitle: A record of what was grown
how.whatBody: For your district and season, AgriSense lists the crops that held the largest share of recorded cropped area in past years. The percentage is that historical share. A high figure means the crop has been widely grown there, not that it will suit your field this year.
how.dataBody: The guide uses historical district-level crop area records. Recent years count for more than older years. When a district has too few records, the state's pattern is used and the guide tells you so.
how.weatherBody: Current conditions and the 7-day forecast come from Open-Meteo. Each panel shows whether the data is live, cached or unavailable, and when it was fetched. Weather does not change the ranking.
how.soilBody: You can store soil test values on a field if you wish. They are kept for your reference and are not used by the Regional Crop Guide.
how.limitsBody: It cannot predict yield or prices, give fertilizer amounts, or replace advice from your local agriculture office. Use it as one input alongside local knowledge.

why.title: About this ranking
why.lead: How the guide was put together, in plain language.
why.methodBody: Crops are ordered by their share of recorded cropped area in your district for this season. The data service describes the basis as: {basis}.
why.weightTitle: How much of it is your district
why.weightBody: District records carry {weight}% of the weight. {records} district records were available, covering {years} years between {first} and {last}.
why.fallbackBody: Because district records were limited, the pattern for {state} was blended in. The state's pattern may differ from your district's.
why.recencyBody: More recent seasons are given more weight than older ones, so a change in what farmers grow shows up gradually.

notAvailable.title: This is not available yet
notAvailable.predictionWhy: AgriSense does not yet have a validated yield model, so it will not show a crop prediction. A number without that validation would only look precise.
notAvailable.predictionMeanwhile: In the meantime the Regional Crop Guide shows what has historically been grown in your district.
notAvailable.fertilizerWhy: Fertilizer guidance needs a verified source and a soil test for your field. AgriSense has neither in place, so it does not show fertilizer amounts.
notAvailable.fertilizerMeanwhile: Your local soil health office or the official portals under Government Schemes can help you get a soil test and advice.
notAvailable.marketWhy: Live market prices need a verified data provider. AgriSense has not connected one, so it shows no prices rather than guessing.
notAvailable.marketMeanwhile: For current prices please check your local mandi or an official source.
